findings.interpretation: Static mechanism density demonstrates complexity and interaction substrate, but cannot establish whether intended interactions or progression are legible. Player reports and creator fixes identify exactly those failures.
benchmark_action: retain command/redstone density only as mechanism-complexity/context, not quality

findings.interpretation: Absence of normal survival resources near spawn is expected for an authored adventure/collectathon start and must not become a negative quality signal. The nearby chest is more relevant to the intended interaction profile.
benchmark_action: make resource/progression expectations conditional on declared gameplay profile
distinguish survival-start feasibility from authored-adventure feasibility
add collectible/hint/goal affordance metrics for adventure profiles
never aggregate profile-inapplicable metrics into a general score

blind_observation.camera_lane: official 26.3 client tour qualified on generated reference world, reusable after version-compatible treatment

findings.interpretation: Player praise for scenery, decoration, music, relaxation and enjoyment is not explained by the current resource/biome static analyzer. This is an evidence-backed reason to add visual/audio/theme analysis, while keeping relaxation/fun as human-primary outcomes.
benchmark_action: test visual/audio proxies against held-out human reports
do not directly score relaxation, immersion or fun

falsification_questions: Can a mechanically dense map be highly legible, falsifying any simple complexity->confusion rule?
Can an adventure map with no survival resources receive strong human approval because resources are profile-inapplicable?
Can visual-coherence metrics distinguish a praised authored environment from a visually incoherent but mechanically valid one?
Do persona stall/backtrack metrics predict reported confusion after controlling for puzzle difficulty and player skill?
disposition: Use these as benchmark-development hypotheses; do not change Concept Authority or produce an overall quality score from two worlds.
